name: Kanxue (看雪) Security Forum
summary: 看雪 (Kanxue) is a major Chinese-language security research forum founded in 2000, focused heavily on reverse engineering, binary vulnerabilities, packing/unpacking, Android/iOS security, and CTF, alongside a security job board. It is community-run under the Kanxue/pediy brand and has grown into one of the largest Chinese infosec forums with nearly a million registered members. It best suits Chinese-speaking intermediate-to-advanced practitioners interested in reverse engineering and binary security rather than newcomers looking for beginner hand-holding.
rules_note: Forum uses a temporary-to-formal member progression system for full posting/download privileges; site returned 403 to direct fetch so details are based on search results.
candidate_notes: Affinity: non-english; org: bbs.kanxue.com; join: free-signup; scope: security. Major Chinese reverse-engineering / software security forum founded 2000, sections for reverse engineering, Android/iOS security, CTF, etc. Site blocked direct WebFetch (403), so registration flow and any QQ-group link could not be visually confirmed — based on search-result description only.

name: Kaouenn-noz
summary: Kaouenn-noz is a biohackerspace and DIY-science collective based in Rennes, France, focused on bioart, biohacking, biodesign, and hands-on life-science and environmental projects (such as a water-quality initiative called Hack2Eaux). It suits people interested in citizen science and biology-adjacent hacking more than traditional infosec, and coordinates through a shared Matrix biohacking room.
rules_note: Matrix room (#diybio-biohacking:matrix.org) is a general DIY-bio room shared across groups, not exclusive to this space.
candidate_notes: Hackerspace in Rennes, Brittany, France; founded 2014/09/01. Chat link found via wiki (hackerspaces.org wiki / SpaceAPI / site crawl).  We are individuals who gather and assemble not satisfied with four walls and a roof. We light campfires to practice techniques together, we survey the sciences in and with the living, we revisit tech

name: OpenSage
summary: OpenSage is an open-source framework for building AI agents that can autonomously develop and train other agents, and the team behind it built SageCTF, an AI agent that competed in a CTF at DEF CON 2026. The Discord is a small discussion space for the underlying software (agent development kit, inference/training tooling) rather than a general security-learning community, so it mainly suits developers already working on AI-driven offensive security tooling.
candidate_notes: Academic CTF team on CTFtime (https://ctftime.org/team/429571, country US, academic flag True); Discord link found on the team website.
